title: Lower bound on check failure probability
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $w_0,\\ldots,w_{n-1}$ be Boolean values, and let $P$ assign Boolean values to product positions $X_0,\ldots,X_{n-1}$ and prefix positions $L_0,\ldots,L_n$ and $Q_0,\ldots,Q_n$. Consider the $3n+3$ checks consisting of $L_0=0$, $Q_0=0$, and $Q_n=1$, together with, for each $i<n$, the checks $L_i+w_i=L_{i+1}$ modulo $2$, $X_i=L_i\land w_i$, and $Q_i+X_i=Q_{i+1}$ modulo $2$. If at least one of these checks fails, then a uniformly chosen check fails with probability at least $1/(3n+3)$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean assignment to the product and prefix positions
